label: The opening piece of a strong verdict (good or bad) that is split into several tokens, lighting up on that first piece before the rest arrives: hyphenated verdict compounds (ground-breaking, mind-blowing, jaw-dropping, mouth-watering, world-class, first-class, state-of-the-art), verdict set phrases (out of this world, second to none), strong verdicts written in ALL CAPS (FANTASTIC, INCREDIBLE, HORRIBLE), and foreign strong verdicts that split (German unglaublich, außergewöhnlich; French hors norme; Russian замечательный). Strongest right after is/was/a, and also fires before a noun (a mouth-watering roast). Quiet on the same opening words used literally (broke his jaw, a hair-band, the ground floor), on neutral or mild hyphenated words (hand-made, water-proof, well-written, ill-conceived, over-priced, so-so), and on strong verdicts written as one ordinary lowercase token (fantastic, incredible, wonderful). Bare 'state' and 'ground' in non-verdict uses can fire weakly.

probed_before.source: this checkout's .probe-log, before the pre-registration commit

qc.label_under_test: The opening piece of a strong verdict (good or bad) that is still unfinished, in a judging slot after is/was/a: it lights up on the first piece of a split or hyphenated verdict word or set phrase, already before the rest arrives (was truly ground-breaking, was mind-blowing, was jaw-dropping, was out of this world, a first-class job, INC-REDIBLE / HORRIBLE in ALL CAPS, German war außergewöhnlich, French était hors norme, Russian зам-ечательный). Quiet on the same opening words in literal uses (turned the ground over, a ground-floor shed, walked out of the room, changed her mind, broke his jaw), on strong verdicts written as one ordinary token (incredible, extraordinary, wonderful), on finished intensifiers (absolutely, extremely), and on mild verdicts (okay, fine, gut). Exception: German außerhalb ('outside') also fires on its opening piece.
